title: Vancouver, WA Insulation Rebates 2026: Clark Public Utilities Per-Foot Rebates
desc: Vancouver, Washington insulation rebates for 2026: Clark Public Utilities pays $0.75 per square foot for attics and floors, $1.20 for walls and $200 to $500 for duct sealing.
lead: Clark Public Utilities pays $0.75 per square foot for floor and attic insulation and $1.20 per square foot for walls, if the existing insulation is thin. It also pays $200 or $500 for sealing ducts.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Vancouver, Washington
cards_intro: We read Clark Public Utilities' weatherization page on October 6, 2026. The rebates are for existing electrically heated single-family homes and manufactured homes. Clark says it also offers income-qualified versions of some of these rebates.

cards.title: Attic insulation
cards.note: Existing insulation must be R-19 or less. New insulation must reach R-38 or R-49.

cards.title: Floor insulation
cards.note: Existing insulation must be R-11 or less. New insulation must reach R-19, R-25 or R-30.

cards.title: Wall insulation
cards.note: For walls that have not been done before, with no existing insulation. New insulation must reach R-11.

cards.title: Duct sealing
cards.note: A prescriptive rebate. The page lists the amount as $200 or $500 and we did not read which jobs get which.

cards.title: State help for lower incomes
cards.note: The state's home electrification program covers heat pumps and wiring, not insulation. For insulation help, ask your community action agency about weatherization.

after_cards:
Working it out

Suppose a Vancouver house has a 1,000 square foot attic at R-11 and a 1,000 square foot floor at R-11. At $0.75 per square foot each, the rebates are $750 plus $750, or $1,500. If 1,200 square feet of walls with no insulation are filled, add 1,200 times $1.20, or $1,440. Together that is $2,940. Your actual areas are measured by the contractor.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says about 40 percent of homes in Vancouver, Washington were built before 1980, and only about 5 percent before 1940. About 27 percent were built in 2000 or later. Clark's rebates only pay when your existing insulation is thin, so a newer home may not qualify. The utility's own page says new homes are required to have R-49 insulation in the ceiling and R-30 in the floor over unconditioned space. If your attic is already near R-38, you are probably done.

About 68 percent of Vancouver homes heat with electricity. That matters, because the weatherization rebates are for electrically heated homes.

Clark's page makes an honest point. How much more insulation you need depends on the cost of the fuel you use to heat your home. From a purely money view, the less you pay for fuel, the less sense extra insulation makes, so the rebate matters more for an electric home. The utility notes that homes built in the 1960s and 1970s often have little insulation because fuel was cheap then. Check your attic and ask for a measurement before you spend.

The same page pays $40 for an ENERGY STAR insulated exterior door. Ducts are another place for savings. A prescriptive duct sealing rebate pays $200 or $500, and a duct insulation rebate applies when ducts run through unheated space with no insulation. We did not read the full duct rules. Call Clark's energy counselors at 360-992-3355 and ask what applies to your ducts.
claim_heading: How to claim a Vancouver, Washington insulation rebate
claim_steps: Confirm that Clark Public Utilities serves your home and that your main heat is electric.
Ask a contractor to measure your existing insulation and report the R-value for each area.
Compare that with the starting levels on the rebate page.
Keep the final invoice showing square feet and the new R-value.
Apply to the utility and ask about the income-qualified version if your income may qualify.
